cells.tense: You are here with what possibility became, and you are still holding it.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one open possibility and give it a heading this week. One line about where it is meant to go, and one hour spent on it exactly there. If a second option keeps pushing for attention, set it down until the week is out.
cells.core:
You're standing where everything is still possible, and it doesn't scatter you. The field is open and you can see one direction through it clearly. When an option turns up, you can tell whether it takes you along that line, and you can pass it up without feeling robbed. That's what makes the openness usable instead of heavy. Nothing has been cut away. You've simply stopped treating every possibility as an equal claim on you, and what's left moves.

What this balance is free to feed next is that one heading. Pick a single open possibility, say in writing where it's meant to go, and put a real hour behind it this week. Let the other options sit where they are. The aim isn't to close the field; it's to have a direction through it that you can actually walk in. When the week ends, the heading tells you where the time went, and you can choose again.
cells.sheetLine: The field is open, and you're standing in one direction.
cells.place: in the open field before any choice has been made

cells.tense: You are bracing for what this possibility becomes, and you haven't got there yet.
cells.ask: Before you name what's here, look at it for a minute. Write five plain things you can see — no conclusion, no plan, no verdict — and then set it down. Once a day this week is enough.
cells.core:
You can still feel how wide this is, and that's the problem. Something in you has already decided how it turns out, and you're living in that version while the real thing sits here unfinished. You plan past it, you prepare for outcomes that haven't happened, and the rehearsal runs so hard the present can't take a step. The shine the record names is genuine. It's just out in front of what exists, and nothing here gets to surprise you anymore.

Look before you name. For a minute, do nothing but take in what's actually here — the draft, the seed, the person, the room — and write five plain things you can see, with no conclusion attached to any of them. Then stop. The point isn't to reach an answer. It's to let what's here arrive before you tell it what it is, and only once a day, so you aren't turning this into one more task to get ahead of.
cells.sheetLine: The future is brightly rehearsed. What's here hasn't been looked at.
cells.place: in the open field before any choice has been made

cells.tense: Something became real and finished, and you're still standing where it started.
cells.act: sit somewhere new with nothing in your hands and let whatever comes, come
cells.ask: Sit ten minutes somewhere you don't usually sit, hands empty, nothing to search for or decide. Let whatever comes, come. Once is the whole exercise.
cells.core:
You were standing at the beginning of something, and the beginning is behind you now. What's gone is the feel of possibility — the sense that anything could still be chosen. These days the field looks closed, and you hold it carefully, half-thinking you'll walk back into it. You still know how it felt. You aren't in it. Nothing in you is meeting the present while you stand there.

A feeling arrives before you can name it, and a room reaches you whether or not you're looking. Let something in unprepared, without deciding first what it is. Ten minutes somewhere new, nothing to search for or process or record. If nothing comes, ten minutes is still the whole thing. You're not being asked to take an interest or to work on yourself. Sit where the room can reach you and let it, then get up.
cells.sheetLine: You still know the door. You're standing on the other side of it.
cells.place: in the open field before any choice has been made

cells.tense: You keep deciding where this possibility is going, and none of the deciding counts as yours.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring one other person into what usually runs on your judgment alone — one piece, one decision they help you make — and share the credit for where it lands.
cells.core:
You're steering what this possibility becomes, and by your own account you're just going along with what's already there. Plans get made through you — the timing, the size, the direction — and when anyone asks how it was decided, the answer is that it decided itself. Your hand is on it and it isn't on the record. So the work keeps widening while the decisions go unowned, and the ones near you can feel who set the course even when you can't say it.

Step into the work with someone. Choose one connection — one piece of this, one decision, one stretch of the effort — and let two streams run as one for a while: they shape it with you and the credit is shared. You don't have to announce that you've been deciding things. Just let one decision be made with another hand on it, out loud, where you can hear yourself joined to it, so the two of you are answering for where it went.
cells.sheetLine: Your hand is on the course. You say it went that way.
cells.place: in the open field before any choice has been made

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a completion has already occurred and is being carried — the seat says undifferentiated possibility, so I can only say the person is holding something that has finished taking shape, not which thing. A reader could reasonably say nothing has completed, and if so the Too Much and Too Little cells still hold (a future run ahead of a live field; a closed door with nothing arriving through it). The asks survive being wrong because each is one small act on possibility or direction, useful whether or not completion has happened. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'everything the beginning promised' — it sounds like a verdict the person never gave, so the cells leave it out.
